headline: Approved $1,579,693 Highway Facility solar carport contract; referred Old Tower Hill Road Form-Based Code zoning changes to Planning Board.
summary: Council referred proposed Old Tower Hill Road Form-Based Code zoning amendments to the Planning Board after a public hearing. Council approved a solar carport design-build contract, several rate studies, road and utility contracts, and routine licenses. Council continued a regional desalination request to October 26, 2026, with Council Member Bergner voting no.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the September 28, 2026 Work Session. Council Vice President Marran abstained.
Approved the minutes of the September 28, 2026 Regular Session. Council Vice President Marran abstained.
Accepted the minutes of the September 28, 2026 Closed Executive Session. Council Vice President Marran abstained.
Approved a contract with NewGen Strategies & Solutions for a Wastewater Division rate study, not to exceed $19,900.00, unanimous.
Approved a contract with BETA Group, Inc. for Pavement Management Plan support services, not to exceed $9,500, unanimous.
Approved an award to Franklin Paint for road epoxy paint remover, not to exceed $24,435.00, unanimous.
Approved a NEOGOV performance management software and Single Sign-On contract, not to exceed $24,845.85, unanimous.
Approved an award of purchase for a replacement dump truck bed from Douglas Dynamics, Inc., not to exceed $14,510, unanimous.
Approved victualling license renewals for three businesses, beginning December 1, 2026, unanimous.
Approved a Trailer Park/Campground License renewal for Carpenter's Beach Meadow, Inc., beginning December 1, 2026, unanimous.
Approved a Tourist Accommodations License renewal for Mooresfield Estate, LLC, beginning December 1, 2026, unanimous.
Approved the Town Assessor abating taxes of $3,987.72, unanimous.
Approved a new victualling license for Couchey Gourmet LLC d/b/a SoCo and Jawn's, beginning December 1, 2026, unanimous.
Approved a Miscellaneous Permit for the Wakefield Village Association's Halloween Stroll on October 24, 2026, unanimous.
Referred proposed Old Tower Hill Road Form-Based Code zoning amendments to the Planning Board for further review, unanimous.
Approved a design-build contract with RISE Group, Inc. for the Highway Facility solar carport, $1,579,693, with total project authorization not to exceed $1,658,677.65, unanimous.
Approved a contract with NewGen Strategies & Solutions for a Water Division rate management plan, not to exceed $48,900.00, unanimous.
Approved the Town Manager executing a Local Public Agency Agreement with the State of Rhode Island for the 2027 Municipal Road and Bridge Program, unanimous.
Approved a contract with NewGen Strategies & Solutions for a Solid Waste Division rate study, not to exceed $44,800.00, funded by an inter-fund advance from the general fund, unanimous.
Approved an amendment to the E.W. Burman, Inc. Old Mountain Field Improvements contract, from $4,151,460 to $4,251,460, unanimous.
Approved a contract with O'Brien & Sons Inc. for new playground structures at Treaty Rock Park, not to exceed $94,707.06, unanimous.
Approved an additional $12,500 for GZA Geoenvironmental Inc. Noyes Farm Land Management Plan work, raising the contract to not exceed $75,000, unanimous.
Approved a bid award to Dennis K. Burke, Inc. for unleaded gasoline and ultra diesel fuel for a two-year contract with two one-year renewal options, unanimous.
Approved a bid award to Precision Alarm Corp. for fire alarm, sprinkler, and suppression systems service, not to exceed $26,472 for the first year, unanimous.
Received and placed on file an email from Geoffrey Levy in favor of allowing residential and mixed-use properties in Form-Based Code commercial districts, unanimous.
Received and placed on file an email from Scot Hallberg in opposition to proposed Form-Based Code zoning, unanimous.
Continued the letter from Norma Roelke on the Short-Term Rental Ordinance to the October 26, 2026 meeting, by consensus.
Continued the James Brangi request on regional desalination to October 26, 2026 and directed a memo on costs, 4-1 with Council Member Bergner voting no.

REGULAR SESSION 
 
OCTOBER 13, 2026 
 
1 
 
At a REGULAR SESSION of the Town Council of the Town of South Kingstown, County of 
Washington, in the State of Rhode Island held at the Town Hall, in and for said Town on the 13th day 
of October 2026 at 7:43 PM. 
 
 PRESENT: Rory H. McEntee, President  
Michael K. Marran, Vice President 
Deborah D. Bergner 
Patricia A. Alley 
Jay G. Wegimont 
 
1. REGULAR SESSION  
 
A. Pledge of Allegiance 
 
The Pledge of Allegiance is given. 
 
B. Land Acknowledgement Statement  
 
The Land Acknowledgement Statement is read. 
 
2. ROLL CALL 
 
Roll Call is taken and all members are present. 
 
3. APPROVAL OF MINUTES OF PREVIOUS MEETINGS 
 
A. Work Session: VOTED: that the minutes of the Work Session held on September 28, 2026 
are accepted, approved, and placed on file. 
 
Council Vice President Marran abstains. 
 
B. Regular Session: VOTED: that the minutes of the Regular Session held on September 28, 
2026 are accepted, approved, and placed on file. 
 
Council Vice President Marran abstains. 
 
C. Closed Executive Session: VOTED: that the minutes of the Closed Executive Session held 
on September 28, 2026 are accepted.  
 
Council Vice President Marran abstains. 
 
6. CONSENT AGENDA 
 
UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to approve the Consent Agenda as indicated by (CA) on same. 
 
(CA) A. UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to authorize an award to NewGen Strategies & Solutions, 
900 Bestfate Road, Suite 402, Annapolis, MD 21401 for the Wastewater Division, Rate Study, in an 
amount not to exceed $19,900.00, which includes a $5,000.00 contingency, from the Sewer Division 
Enterprise Fund, Unrestricted Net Assets, as further described in a purchasing recommendation from

Division, Rate Study." 
 
(CA) B. UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to authorize an award to BETA Group, Inc., 701 George 
Washington Highway, Lincoln, RI 02865 for Pavement Management Plan Support Services, in an 
amount not to exceed $9,500 which includes a $2,000 contingency, with an optional 1-year extension 
no greater than 5% increase, from Department of Public Services, Capital Reserve Fund 418, Project 
26009, as further described in a purchasing recommendation from the Director of Public Services to 
the Town Manager dated October 2, 2026, regarding "Pavement Management Plan Support 
Services." 
 
(CA) C. UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to authorize an award to Franklin Paint, 259 Cottage St., 
Franklin, MA 02038 for Road Epoxy Paint Remover, in an amount not to exceed $24,435.00, from 
Public Services, Highway Division, Equipment Reserve, account number 40830001 -550006-
PW015, as further described in a purchasing recommendation from the Director of Public Services 
to the Town Manager dated October 5, 2026, regarding "Award of Purchase Recommendation, 
Grindlazer System Carbide.” 
 
(CA) D. UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to authorize an award of contract to 
GovernmentJobs.com, Inc., d/b/a NEOGOV, 2120 Park Place, Suite 100, El Segundo, CA 90245, 
for the purchase, setup, implementation, and subscription of the NEOGOV Perform performance

through Sourcewell  Contract No. 030425 -PDMS, with funding available in the Personnel 
Administration's Computer / Software Maintenance account, as further described in a memorandum 
from the Deputy Town Manager/Director of Administrative Services to the Town Manager dated 
September 18, 2026, entitled “Recommendation for Purchase Award – NEOGOV Perform 
Performance Management Software and Single Sign-On.” 
 
(CA) E. UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to authorize an award of purchase of a replacement dump 
truck bed to Douglas Dynamics, INC, DBA: Dejana Truck & Utility Equipment Co. Inc. in an amount 
not to exceed $14,510, from Parks and Recreation Vehicle Repair Fund 40840000-490408-PR009,

A. Julie Couchey is present and after testimony and discussion it is 
 
UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to grant a Victualling License for the year beginning December 1, 2026 to 
Couchey Gourmet LLC d/b/a SoCo  and Jawn’s, 1227 Kingstown Road, Wakefield, RI 02879. 
Application by Dean Couchey, Owner. New; License No. 95022. 
 
B. Peg Gregoire and Rebekah Cook are present and after testimony and discussion it is 
 
UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to grant a Miscellaneous Permit to conduct the Halloween Stroll on 
Saturday, October 24, 2026, from 12:00 PM to 3:00 PM at Saugatucket Park, Wakefield, RI 02879 
to the Wakefield Village Association, PO Box 174, Wakefield, RI 02880, subject to the execution of 
a hold harmless agreement indemnifying the Town and receipt of a Certificate of Insurance naming 
the Town as an additional insured for the events in the amounts specified by the Finance Director. 
Application by Peg Gregoire, Treasurer. New; Special Events License No. 95118. 
 
8. PUBLIC COMMENTS – 30 MINUTES 
 
Council President McEntee invites residents to come forward with comments. 
 
John Impagliazzo comments on potential installation of sewer connections on Narragansett Avenue 
East. 
 
Bob Trager comments on his recent travels through Europe and the rise of AI technology. 
 
9. PUBLIC HEARING 
 
A. Notice having been duly given, a Public Hearing continued from September 14 and 
September 28, 2026, is held to consider proposed amendments to the Zoning Ordinance, Appendix 
A: Article 6, New Section 610, to implement Old Tower Hill Road Form -Based Code (FBC) and 
establish five (5) Form-Based Districts, as shown on the following Regulating Plan Map and viewable 
in its entirety on the Town's website at: https://www.southkingstownri.gov/othr-fbc. 
 
The FBC provides a regulatory framework that supports a walkable, mixed -use, and context -
sensitive suburban/urban environment in the Old Tower Hill Road area. The amendments set forth 
when the FBC standards apply, define the scope of compliance with those standards, and establish 
the review process and application requirements for development applications within the FBC 
Districts.
REGULAR SESSION 
 
OCTOBER 13, 2026 
 
4 
 
Amendment to the Zoning Ordinance – Old Tower Hill Road Form-Based Code   
(Zoning Ordinance, Appendix A: Article 6, New Sec. 610) 
 
 
 
James Rabbitt, Planning Director, presents proposed modifications to FBC to eliminate FB1, modify 
FB2 areas, and clarify FBC language. He displays renderings of reconfigured FBC districts with FB1 
districts removed and two small FB2 districts removed. Text language is modified in 7A. Purpose to 
confirm mandatory FBC Zoning and 7F. Parking Standards to add new secti ons 3(a) to reduce 
parking requirements by 50% in FB1.5 and FB2 and 3(b) to reduce parking by 25% in FB3. 
 
Discussion ensues relative to  vertical additions to existing buildings, encouraging local small 
business, reducing the auto-centric downtown area, adding gas stations as a n accepted use, 
removal of FB1, and optional versus mandatory FBC. 
 
Amy Goins, Assistant Town Solicitor, notes that optional Zoning standards do not exist in Rhode 
Island and clarifies development that would trigger FBC. 
 
The Planning Director notes that optional FBC would make it difficult to achieve long term goals. 
 
Discussion ensues in regard to expanding affordable housing through FBC, the historic goals of the 
Economic Development Committee from 2018 not being reflected in the current proposed FBC, 
removing all residential districts from FBC or preparing a phased approach to the districts, and public-
private spaces mandated through FBC. 
 
The Planning Director responds.
REGULAR SESSION 
 
OCTOBER 13, 2026 
 
5 
 
Discussion ensues relative to stormwater management concerns, potential continuance of the Public 
Hearing to consider other specific concerns, and the addition of further clarifying language. 
 
The Town Solicitor recommends continuing the Public Hearing to a future meeting, date uncertain, 
with enough time to allow the Planning Board to make modifications and re-notice residents. 
 
Council President McEntee invites residents to come forward with comments. 
 
Larry Fish comments on legacy commercial property owners’ local contributions, the potential for out 
of state large corporations to purchase properties, and the FBC development process. 
 
Jordan Towle comments in favor of FBC and creating a walkable downtown area. 
 
Robert Thompson comments in favor of FBC and cautions careful consideration of FBC regulations 
in residential districts. 
 
Veronika Kot comments in favor of removing residential districts from FBC and setting restrictions in 
current residential districts, and expresses concerns relative to increasing residential density. 
 
Barbara Lema comments relative to imposing development restrictions in residential Zoning districts. 
 
James Moriarty comments in opposition to FBC.  
 
Joe Viele comments in favor of continuing the FBC Public Hearing to allow the Planning Board to 
make modifications to the proposed code. 
 
Attorney Matthew Landry comments in opposition to FBC and the need for clarifying language in the 
proposed code. 
 
Discussion ensues relative to long term impacts of FBC to commercial property owners’ investments. 
 
The Town Solicitor clarifies that relief is always available to property owners through application to 
the Zoning or Planning Board for Dimensional and Use Variances. 
 
Bob Trager comments in favor of increasing affordable housing in Town. 
 
Fran Alexakos comments in opposition to FBC. 
 
Josh Daly comments in favor of increasing affordable housing and the need to be forward thinking. 
 
Mike Gagas, Economic Development Committee, comments in favor of FBC  and commercial 
development providing potential tax relief to residents. 
 
John Reiner comments in favor of FBC , the need for Zoning changes in the Town  to allow for 
additional housing, and the ability to make further changes in the future. 
 
Madeleine Blackman comments in support of FBC. 
 
Kristina Brown, Executive Director of Neighbors Welcome!, comments in support of FBC.
REGULAR SESSION 
 
OCTOBER 13, 2026 
 
6 
 
Discussion ensues relative to removal of FB1.5 and FB2 districts that don’t front on Kingstown Road 
and Old Tower Hill Road. 
 
UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to close the Public Hearing. 
 
The Town Solicitor recommends that the Town Council direct the Planning Board or Planning 
Department to convene a meeting with local property owners. 
 
Discussion ensues relative to modification directives to the Planning Board regarding FBC district 
boundaries fronting major corridors, stormwater management, vertical development, permitted uses, 
engaging with local business owners, thresholds that trigger compliance, and implementing optional 
FBC for a certain time period. 
 
The Planning Director reviews the timeline to bring the proposed Form-Based Code amendments 
back to Council. 
 
Discussion ensues and it is 
 
UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to refer to the Planning Board proposed amendments to the Zoning 
Ordinance, Appendix A: Article 6, New Section 610, to implement Old Tower Hill Road Form-Based 
Code (FBC) for further review of the five (5) Form -Based Districts, stormwater maintenance, use 
codes, and compliance thresholds, as shown on the following Regulating Plan Map and viewable in 
its entirety on the Town's website at: https://www.southkingstownri.gov/othr-fbc. 
 
Amendment to the Zoning Ordinance – Old Tower Hill Road Form-Based Code   
(Zoning Ordinance, Appendix A: Article 6, New Sec. 610)
REGULAR SESSION 
 
OCTOBER 13, 2026 
 
7 
 
10. NEW BUSINESS 
 
A. Lucas Murray, Deputy Town Manager/DOAS, reviews a request for a solar canopy at the 
Highway Department Facilities. 
 
Discussion ensues and it is 
 
UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to authorize the Town Manager to award a Design-Build contract to RISE 
Group, Inc., 1341 Elmwood Avenue, Cranston, Rhode Island 02910, for the design, permitting, 
procurement, construction, utility interconnection, commissioning and closeout of the Highway 
Facility Solar Carport Project, in the base amount of One Million Five Hundred Eighteen Thousand 
Twenty-Two Dollars ($1,518,022), together with acceptance of the domestic -content equipment 
alternate in the amount of Sixty -One Thousand Six Hundred Seventy -One Dollars ( $61,671), 
resulting in a total contract amount of One Million Five Hundred Seventy-Nine Thousand Six Hundred 
Ninety-Three Dollars ($1,579,693), and further authorizing a Town-controlled contingency equal to 
5% of the contract amount, or Seventy-Eight Thousand Nine Hundred Eighty-Four Dollars and Sixty-
Five Cents ($78,984.65), for a total project authorization not to exceed One Million Six Hundred Fifty-
Eight Thousand Six Hundred Seventy-Seven Dollars and Sixty-Five Cents ($1,658,677.65), with 
expenditures from the contingency limited to unforeseen conditions, necessary changes in the Work 
or other project -related costs authorized by the Town Manager in accordance with the Town’s 
purchasing requirements, subject to final contract negotiations, confirmation of financing, approval 
of the contract documents by the Town Solicitor, and the contractor’s submission of all required 
insurance, performance and payment bonds and other pre-construction documentation, as further 
described in a memorandum from the Deputy Town Manager/Director of Administrative Services to 
the Town Manager dated October 8, 2026, entitled “Award of Design-Build Contract for the Highway 
Facility Solar Carport Project.” 
 
B. UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to authorize an award to NewGen Strategies & Solutions, 900 
Bestfate Road, Suite 402, Annapolis, MD 21401 for the Water Division, Water Rate Management 
Plan, in an amount not to exceed $48,900.00, which includes a $5,000.00 contingency, from the 
Water Division Enterprise Fund, Unrestricted Net Assets, as further described in a purchasing 
recommendation from the Director of Public Services to the Town Manager dated October 1, 2026, 
regarding "Water Rate Management Plan and Rate Study." 
 
C. UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to authorize the Town Manager to execute a Local Public Agency 
Agreement with the State of Rhode Island, in accordance with terms of the agreement as approved 
by the Town Solicitor and as further detailed in a memorandum from the Public Services Director to 
the Town Manager dated October 1, 2026, and entitled "2027 Municipal Road and Bridge Program, 
Local Public Agency Agreement." 
 
D. UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to authorize an award to NewGen Strategies & Solutions, 900 
Bestfate Road, Suite 402, Annapolis, MD 21401 for the Solid Waste Division, Rate Study, in an 
amount not to exceed $44,800.00, which includes a $5,000.00 contingency.  This award would be 
funded through an inter-fund advance from the general fund, recorded as a "D ue to the General 
Fund" liability within the Solid Waste Fund.  The Solid Waste Fund will reimburse the general fund 
as funding becomes available through solid waste revenues, grants, financing proceeds or other 
dedicated fund resources, as further described in a purchasing recommendation from the Director of 
Public Services to the Town Manager dated October 1, 2026, regarding "Solid Waste Division, Rate 
Study."
REGULAR SESSION 
 
OCTOBER 13, 2026 
 
8 
 
E. Theresa Murphy, Director of Leisure Services,  reviews a request for construction of Old 
Mountain Field improvements  and an expanded scope of work for the Noyes Farm Land

UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to authorize an amendment to an award of contract to E.W. Burman, Inc.

G. UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to authorize to amend a contract, originally authorized on March

H. Brian Silvia, Finance Director, reviews a request for the purchase and delivery of unleaded
